title: ARPA-H
funder: Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H), U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
deadline_note: Mission Office ISOs take Solution Summaries on a rolling basis; each solicitation states it will remain open until March 5, 2029 (also the Solution Summary deadline). A full proposal is requested within 45 calendar days of receiving Solution Summary feedback unless ARPA-H gives another timeline.

summary.at_a_glance: ARPA-H funds high-risk health R&D through Other Transaction agreements, not grants. The always-open route is one of four Mission Office ISOs on SAM.gov (Health Science Futures ARPA-H-SOL-24-104, Proactive Health ARPA-H-SOL-24-106, Scalable Solutions ARPA-H-SOL-24-105, Resilient Systems ARPA-H-SOL-24-103): submit a six-page Solution Summary on the ARPA-H Solutions site, wait for written feedback, then submit a full proposal.
summary.what_they_offer: Milestone-based Other Transaction (OT) awards for individual research projects that fall outside existing ARPA-H programs; multiple awards are anticipated and no dollar range is stated. Resource sharing may be encouraged or requested. ARPA-H strives to give written Solution Summary feedback within thirty (30) business days and to respond to proposals within sixty (60) calendar days. Separately, ARPA-H runs time-limited Program ISOs and SBIR/STTR awards (contracts of up to $600K for Phase 1 and $3.5M for Phase 2); on 2026-11-24 the ARPA-H site said there were no open small business opportunities.
summary.what_theyre_looking_for: Revolutionary, not incremental, advances. Proactive Health Office interest areas (ARPA-H-SOL-24-106, Amendment 04): novel prevention, detection and prophylactic treatment methods (including continuous, population-scale sensing of health state and low/no-cost early detection); population-level approaches to increase adoption of prevention and wellness behaviors; system innovation for delivering proactive health outcomes. Excluded: incremental advances, technology at the clinical trial stage, policy changes, traditional education and training, center formation, and physical infrastructure. Proposal evaluation criteria in descending order of importance: (1) Overall Scientific and Technical Merit, (2) Potential Contribution and Relevance to the ARPA-H Mission, (3) Proposer's Capabilities and/or Related Experience, (4) Cost/Price/Budget Assessment.
summary.who_can_apply: All responsible sources capable of satisfying the government's needs: academia, non-profit organizations, for-profit entities (small businesses included), hospitals, community health centers, non-federal research centers. FFRDCs and government entities cannot be team members. ARPA-H prioritizes entities that conduct the funded work in the U.S.; no award to a foreign entity of concern, a party to a malign foreign talent recruitment program, or a suspended/debarred entity. Entities currently providing contracted support services to ARPA-H are ineligible. SAM.gov registration and a UEI are required at proposal submission, not for the Solution Summary.
summary.how_to_apply: 1) Read ARPA-H's Program and Initiatives portfolio and confirm the idea is outside it. 2) Pick the one Mission Office ISO that fits best and download the solicitation PDF, the Appendix A Solution Summary template and the Bundle of Attachments from SAM.gov. 3) Sign in to the ARPA-H Solutions site with a Google or Microsoft account. 4) Submit a Solution Summary (six pages, Appendix A template) through the five-step form: Solution Summary Information, Budget Information, Organizations & Key Personnel, File Uploads, Review & Submit. 5) Receive written feedback encouraging or discouraging a proposal. 6) Register in SAM.gov and obtain a UEI. 7) Submit the full proposal (Technical & Management Proposal of 20 pages, Task Description Document, Cost Proposal, Cost Proposal Workbook, Administrative & National Policy Requirements Document) on the Solutions site. 8) Notice of selection, then award negotiation.
summary.worth_noting: Submit the Solution Summary to only one Mission Office ISO. A submission may be rejected if it is within the scope of an existing ARPA-H program or initiative. ARPA-H says it generally reviews Program/Initiative submissions more quickly than Mission Office ISO submissions. Submitted content cannot be edited. ARPA-H's 'Know Before Applying' guide names three Mission Offices (Health Science Futures, Proactive Health, Scalable Solutions) while the Open Funding Opportunities page and SAM.gov still list a fourth active ISO for the Resilient Systems Office. Program ISOs open on 2026-11-24: SURPASS (ARPA-H-SOL-26-164; Solution Summary due November 30, 2026, proposal due January 22, 2027) and SPECTRA (ARPA-H-SOL-26-163; TA1 & TA2 Solution Summaries due December 2, 2026 3:00PM ET, TA3 due January 19, 2027); EHI and UNIQUE only accept proposals from applicants who met earlier Solution Summary deadlines. Program ISOs have their own templates and limits, which were not captured here.

portal.platform: ARPA-H Solutions site (custom ARPA-H web application at solutions.arpa-h.gov)
portal.notes: Sign-in is only through Google or Microsoft ('Continue with Google' / 'Continue with Microsoft'); there is no separate username/password. Pressing 'Start Submission' while signed out redirects to /login?url=submit-summary. The site loads Google reCAPTCHA Enterprise (invisible). Five-step form with a draft that is saved automatically as you move between steps ('Save Draft and Exit' is offered). Organizations and Key Personnel are added as records first, then picked from dropdowns as Primary Organization and Technical/Administrative Points of Contact. The Solution Summary itself is uploaded as one file (Excel, PDF, Word or PowerPoint, max 500 MB). Submission is final and cannot be edited; after submitting, status is not shown on the site and questions go through 'Ask a Question'. Some opportunities enable extra or video uploads (MP4 up to 10 minutes plus captions file).

questions_note: Three groups, in this order. (1) The Solution Summary document: every field and section heading of 'Appendix A - ARPA-H Solutions Summary Template-Amend-3.docx', downloaded from the active SAM.gov notices (the same file is attached to all four Mission Office ISOs); wording is verbatim, the narrative sections are auto-numbered 1 to 5 in Word, and the six-page limit applies to the whole Solution Summary, not per section. Format rule from the template: English, sans serif font no smaller than 11-point. (2) The web form on the ARPA-H Solutions site: the form sits behind Google/Microsoft sign-in and was NOT seen rendered; labels, help text, options and limits were read from the site's publicly served JavaScript bundle (main-TFKS7EU2.js), so the wording is the site's own but on-screen order inside each step, the options of server-loaded dropdowns (opportunity list, state, country, organization and contact pickers) and which optional uploads appear for a given opportunity could not be confirmed. Organization Type options are listed in code order; the page applies a sort. Fields marked 'SBIR/STTR opportunities only' are added by the code only when the selected opportunity is a small business program. (3) The five full-proposal components, verbatim from section 4.4 of the Proactive Health Office ISO (Amendment 04, June 10, 2026); they apply only after written Solution Summary feedback. The ISO text and evaluation criteria were read from the Proactive Health Office ISO; the Scalable Solutions, Health Science Futures and Resilient Systems ISOs (Amendment 3) show the same deadline, the same 20-page proposal limit and the same template but their interest areas differ. Program ISO and SBIR templates were not captured.

questions.section: Solution Summary document (Appendix A template) — narrative sections (whole Solution Summary limited to six (6) pages; citations do not count)
questions.help: Describe the solution summary concept with minimal jargon and explain how it addresses the ISO interest areas.

questions.section: Solution Summary document (Appendix A template) — narrative sections (whole Solution Summary limited to six (6) pages; citations do not count)
questions.help:
Clearly identify the outcome(s) sought and/or the problem(s) to be solved with the proposed technology concept. Describe how the proposed effort represents an innovative and potentially revolutionary solution to the ISO interest areas. Explain the concept’s potential to be disruptive compared to existing or emerging technologies and how the proposed approach will go far beyond current existing capabilities. To the extent possible, provide quantitative metrics in a table that compares the proposed technology concept to current and emerging technologies which may include:
- A progression of increasingly complex technical challenges.
- State of the art / emerging technology “baseline.”
- Aggressive metrics for each year of the proposed project.
- Summary of specific outcomes from the proposed project or concept.

questions.section: Solution Summary document (Appendix A template) — narrative sections (whole Solution Summary limited to six (6) pages; citations do not count)
questions.help:
Describe the final deliverable(s) for the project, key interim milestones, and the overall technical approach used to achieve project objectives. Discuss alternative approaches considered, if any, and why the proposed approach is most appropriate for the project objectives. Describe the background, theory, simulation, modeling, experimental data, or other sound engineering and scientific practices or principles that support the proposed approach. Provide specific examples of supporting data and/or appropriate citations to the scientific and technical literature. Identify adoption challenges to be overcome for the proposed technology to be successful. Describe why the proposed effort is a significant technical challenge and the key technical risks. At a minimum, the solution summary should address:
- Does the approach require one or more entirely new technical developments to succeed?
- How will technical risk be mitigated?
- What use cases, capabilities, or demonstrations will be featured?

questions.section: Solution Summary document (Appendix A template) — narrative sections (whole Solution Summary limited to six (6) pages; citations do not count)
questions.help:
Indicate the roles and responsibilities of the organizations and key personnel that comprise the Project Team.

Provide the name, position, and institution of each key team member and describe in 1-2 sentences the skills and experience they bring to the team. Key team members include the individuals who are expected to contribute to the scientific development or execution of the project in a substantive, measurable way.
